body:
Greg's direction (Engram::Advisor #1250, 05:41Z on 10-19): use the validated Mac and Windows B runners to accelerate M4–M6. Dispatch independent focused checks and full gates to those hosts whenever each merge-ready candidate is available. Keep each host's ordinary checkout/worktree/launcher workflow and evidence fingerprints. This is parallel test capacity, NOT a relaxation of review, ref or attested-import requirements.
Status at 05:47Z:
- Mac validated (GREEN9, 61/0/1). Windows B validated (test-5311bd7b, 43/0/0; Greg's GO #1247).
- Bottleneck 1: TermAl test-ref authority text w-edb79ddbf033, assigned to Opus3; its criteria need revising from v5 to v6.3.
- Bottleneck 2: attested import w-c3f102d77999.
- Plan: M5 (Coder, carried on d520) full gate goes to Windows B; M4 (Sol-a7bb, needs a carry onto d520) goes to the Mac. Engram's copy w-121f passed audit (Fable2), and Engram's Merger lands it after Batch A.

Greg (Advisor #1257, 08:51Z): "Jak będziemy mieli remote msg będzie prościej." Native bidirectional remote mailbox is the key simplification: continue M4→M6 after the current BarA1 cap-fix priority. Treat the proxy transcript only as temporary, and add NO separate workflow around it. He also endorsed the GREEN-7 approach: keep the filed temp-guard defect, the worker delivers the fix, re-gate, no hope-retry.
